questions.question: The famous bronze statue of the 'Dancing Girl' was unearthed from which Harappan city?
questions.explanation: The iconic bronze figurine of the Dancing Girl, cast using the lost-wax technique, was discovered at Mohenjodaro.

questions.question: What type of stone was primarily used to manufacture Harappan cubical weights?
questions.explanation: Harappan weights were usually made of a stone called chert and were generally cubical with no markings.

questions.question: Which Harappan site located in Gujarat was situated on Khadir Beyt in the Great Rann of Kutch?
questions.explanation: Dholavira is situated on Khadir Beyt island in the Great Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: The founder of the Mauryan Empire in the fourth century BCE was:
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in c. 321 BCE with the guidance of Chanakya.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: The famous Sanskrit political treatise 'Arthashastra' is traditionally attributed to:
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra was authored by Kautilya (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta), the prime minister of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Megasthenes was an ambassador sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by which Greek ruler?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by the Seleucid king Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In ancient Indian society, tracing descent through the father to son, grandson, and so on is defined as:
questions.explanation: Patriliny means tracing descent from father to son, grandson, and onwards; matriliny traces descent through the mother.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: The practice of a woman having several husbands simultaneously is termed as:
questions.explanation: Polyandry is the practice of a woman having more than one husband, as exemplified by Draupadi's marriage to the five Pandavas.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: According to the Purusha Sukta hymn of the Rigveda, from which part of the primordial cosmic being did the Kshatriyas emerge?
questions.explanation: The Purusha Sukta describes Brahmanas emerging from the mouth, Kshatriyas from the arms, Vaishyas from the thighs, and Shudras from the feet.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Vardhamana Mahavira is revered as which number Tirthankara in the Jain tradition?
questions.explanation: Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara in Jain tradition (Parshvanatha was the 23rd; Rishabhanatha was the 1st).

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Gautama Buddha attained supreme enlightenment (bodhi) under a peepal tree at which holy site?
questions.explanation: The Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Where did the Buddha deliver his First Sermon, setting in motion the Wheel of Dhamma?
questions.explanation: The Buddha gave his first sermon to his five former companions at the Deer Park in Sarnath near Varanasi.

questions.question: In which city of Central Asia (present-day Uzbekistan) was the medieval scholar Al-Biruni born in 973 CE?
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni was born in Khwarizm (modern-day Karakalpakstan/Uzbekistan) in 973 CE.

questions.question: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta was born in which North African port town?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier, Morocco, into an educated family of legal scholars.

questions.question: The French physician Francois Bernier was closely attached to the court of which Mughal prince as a personal doctor?
questions.explanation: Francois Bernier spent twelve years in India (1656-1668) and served as a physician to Prince Dara Shukoh, the eldest son of Shah Jahan.

questions.question: In early medieval Tamil Nadu, the saints who were staunch devotees of Lord Shiva were known as:
questions.explanation: The Nayanars were devotees of Shiva (63 saints), whereas the Alvars were devotees of Vishnu (12 saints).

questions.question: The sacred hospice or residential center where a Sufi master (pir) lived and taught his disciples was known as:
questions.explanation: A khanqah was a Sufi hospice where the shaikh resided, held spiritual assemblies, and distributed food to visitors.

questions.question: Baba Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Nankana Sahib situated near which river in the Punjab?
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak was born at Nankana Sahib (Rai Bhoi di Talwandi) near the river Ravi in Punjab.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE by two brothers named:
options: D) Saluva Narasimha and Vira Narasimha
questions.explanation: Harihara and Bukka founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra river.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Who was the first surveyor and antiquarian to bring the ruins of Hampi to light in 1800?
questions.explanation: Colonel Colin Mackenzie of the East India Company prepared the first comprehensive survey map of Hampi in 1800.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which deity was worshipped as the principal guardian deity of the kingdom of Vijayanagara?
questions.explanation: Virupaksha (a form of Shiva) was the guardian deity of Vijayanagara, and royal orders were signed in his name.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: The grand chronicle 'Akbar Nama', which includes the Ain-i-Akbari, was composed in the Persian language by:
questions.explanation: Abu'l Fazl, Akbar's court historian and close friend, composed the three volumes of the Akbar Nama.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In seventeenth-century Mughal India, ordinary peasant cultivators were commonly denoted by the Indo-Persian term:
questions.explanation: Peasants in Mughal records were referred to as raiyat (plural riaya) or muzarian, and also as asami or kisan.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: In which year was the Permanent Settlement introduced in Bengal by Governor-General Lord Cornwallis?
questions.explanation: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue was enacted in Bengal in 1793 under Lord Cornwallis.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: The Paharias who inhabited the Rajmahal Hills primarily practiced which form of agriculture?
options: D) Shifting cultivation with a hoe
questions.explanation: The Paharias practiced shifting agriculture (jhum), clearing small patches with hoes and gathering forest produce.

questions.question: On which date did the sepoys at the Meerut cantonment mutiny, marking the formal outbreak of the 1857 Revolt?
questions.explanation: The mutiny began at Meerut on Sunday, 10 May 1857, when sepoys broke into the jail and marched towards Delhi.

questions.question: Which young sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry fired at his British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857?
questions.explanation: Mangal Pandey attacked his British sergeant-major at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was executed in April.

questions.question: Rani Lakshmibai, the heroic leader of the 1857 Revolt, led the defense of which princely state against British forces?
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai led the rebellion at Jhansi after Lord Dalhousie annexed the state under the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.question: At Kanpur, which adopted son of the deposed Peshwa Baji Rao II assumed leadership of the rebel forces in 1857?
questions.explanation: Nana Sahib, the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the revolt at Kanpur after being denied the Peshwa's pension.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in which month and year?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji returned to India in January 1915 after more than two decades in South Africa, celebrated today as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.question: Whom did Mahatma Gandhi regard as his political mentor upon his return to India?
questions.explanation: On Gokhale's advice, Gandhiji spent a year travelling across India by third-class train to understand the realities of the common people.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi launched his first satyagraha on Indian soil in 1917 in Champaran (Bihar) to address the plight of peasants cultivating:
questions.explanation: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 championed the cause of indigo tenant-farmers exploited under the tinkathia system.

questions.question: Who was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly of India in December 1946?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was unanimously elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946.

questions.question: Who served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed Chairman of the seven-member Drafting Committee on 29 August 1947.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was officially adopted and enacted by the Constituent Assembly on which historic date?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was formally adopted on 26 November 1949, and it came into full force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

questions.question: Which of the following grains has NOT been recovered from Harappan archaeological excavations?
questions.explanation: Harappan archaeo-botanical finds include wheat, barley, lentil, chickpea, sesame, and millets (at Gujarat sites). Coffee was unknown.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: In ancient Indian economic life, associations of craftspeople and merchants that regulated production, prices, and training were known as:
questions.explanation: Shrenis were powerful merchant and craft guilds that organized procurement of raw materials, manufacturing, banking, and trade.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: According to the Manusmriti, what was the principal ground on which maternal or paternal ancestral property was divided among sons after the parents' death?
options: A) The state confiscated 50% of the land as death duty
B) The property was divided equally between sons and married daughters
C) The youngest son received the entire estate exclusively
D) The eldest son received a special share, and all sons shared equally
questions.explanation: Under the Manusmriti, paternal estate was divided equally among sons after the parents' death, with a special share reserved for the eldest son; women had no claim on ancestral property.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: The five great vows (pancha mahavrata) undertaken by Jain monks and nuns do NOT include which of the following?
options: B) Abstaining from lying and stealing
C) Mandatory performance of animal sacrifices (yajnas)
questions.explanation: Jain vows are: ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha, and brahmacharya. Animal sacrifices were vehemently opposed.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta noted with great fascination that which female ruler had briefly governed the Delhi Sultanate in the thirteenth century, riding horses with an unveiled face?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta recorded historical traditions about Sultan Raziyya, daughter of Iltutmish, who ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240.

questions.question: The musical assembly of spiritual audition practiced by Sufis of the Chishti order to evoke divine ecstasy is called:
questions.explanation: Sama was the practice of singing mystical poetry accompanied by instruments to induce spiritual trance and communion with the Divine.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The most famous ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, Krishnadeva Raya, belonged to which ruling dynasty?
questions.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty, ruling from 1509 to 1529 during Vijayanagara's zenith.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the Ain-i-Akbari, what were the hereditary landholders who enjoyed superior proprietary rights and collected revenue from peasants called?
questions.explanation: Zamindars were landed elites who exercised rights over rural surplus and maintained military contingents.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Under the Permanent Settlement, what was the statutory share of the assessed revenue that the zamindar was entitled to retain as their commission?
questions.explanation: The revenue assessment was split such that 10/11th went to the East India Company and 1/11th remained with the zamindar.

questions.question: Who was the able general and military strategist of Nana Sahib who fought guerilla warfare against British forces until his capture and execution in 1859?
questions.explanation: Tatya Tope conducted brilliant guerilla warfare across central India before being betrayed, captured, and hanged in April 1859.

questions.question: The tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which galvanized the nation behind Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement, occurred in Amritsar on:
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day), General Dyer ordered troops to fire upon an unarmed gathering inside Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.question: How many days and years did the Constituent Assembly take to draft and finalize the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly held eleven sessions over 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days, meeting on 165 days.

questions.question: Which specific craft installation discovered at Mohenjodaro consisted of two cylindrical chambers connected by a flue, utilized for firing delicate terracotta figurines and faience beads?
questions.explanation: Archaeologists excavated sophisticated updraft pottery and bead kilns with flues, demonstrating controlled pyrotechnology.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: In Ashokan epigraphy, which Major Rock Edict uniquely refers to Ashoka's dispatch of emissaries (dutas) to contemporary Hellenistic kings, including Antiochus, Ptolemy, Antigonus, and Magas?
questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict XIII mentions that Dhammavijaya was achieved in kingdoms as far as 600 yojanas away, naming five Greek rulers.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the military strategy of the Vijayanagara rulers, why did they invest enormous wealth in purchasing high-pedigree Arabian and Central Asian horses from Portuguese and Arab merchants?
options: A) Cavalry was the decisive shock-combat arm in warfare against the Deccan Sultanates, and peninsular India had poor indigenous horse breeding
B) Horses were needed exclusively to pull royal ceremonial chariots during the Mahanavami festival
C) The Rayas operated an international horse auction supplying Ming dynasty China
D) Local elephants had been wiped out by disease across Karnataka
questions.explanation: Control of the horse trade was vital because effective cavalry decided battles with rival Sultanates, and local conditions were unfavorable for breeding.
